name: Jesu
label: Hydra Head
lede: Justin Broadrick ended Godflesh with a song called "Jesu", kept the name for his next band, and spent twenty years slowing metal down until it sounded like a lullaby.

eras.title: Godflesh is dead, long live Jesu
eras.text: The last Godflesh album closes on a track called "Jesu", and the band is gone the following spring. Broadrick keeps the name, and the quiet end of that song shows where he is headed.

years.h: Godflesh's last song is named "Jesu"
years.p: Quiet and melodic, it stays the last original Godflesh song until 2014. [[Justin Broadrick|d547a180-6445-42e8-96d6-aabdb6425ab1]] holds onto the title for whatever comes next.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes a hidden passage at the end of the track as unusually peaceful and melodic for Godflesh. Broadrick had wanted Hymns to be more of a rock album than anything the band made before, and it was their first record cut in a professional studio with an outside producer. Drummer [[Ted Parsons|579dbbfe-100d-41b6-9ab7-4f7146c5d598]] thought both were mistakes.

[[Diarmuid Dalton|3a8877b2-c922-43fa-956f-61b240727280]], who first met Broadrick in 1984, plays Moog and electronics on "Jesu". Promotional material for the new project later carried the line "Godflesh is dead, long live Jesu."

years.h: A breakdown the day before the tour kills Godflesh
years.p: Wikipedia dates the split to April 10, 2002, after Justin Green quit the previous October and Broadrick had a nervous breakdown.
years.xp:
Two weeks before a scheduled tour with Strapping Young Lad and Fear Factory, Green called Broadrick to say he was out. He was tired of opening for young bands and objected to touring an album "manipulated from the outside."

After a short run with Paul Raven on bass, Broadrick had his breakdown the day before leaving for a North American tour. He later called it a "real Brian Wilson moment" and said he was "paralyzed by the stress." Every date was cancelled.

eras.title: Two long records in one year
eras.text: Heart Ache is two songs and Jesu is eight. Ted Parsons and Diarmuid Dalton arrive around the full-length, and by Silver Jesu plays like a band.

years.h: Broadrick plays everything on Heart Ache
years.p: The debut EP, out August 30, 2004, runs two songs and 39 minutes. Guitar, bass, vocals and programming are all him (Dry Run, per Wikipedia).

years.h: Seventy-four minutes of Jesu on Hydra Head
years.p: The debut album, out December 8, 2004, brings in [[Ted Parsons|579dbbfe-100d-41b6-9ab7-4f7146c5d598]] on drums and [[Diarmuid Dalton|3a8877b2-c922-43fa-956f-61b240727280]] on bass for some tracks.
years.xp:
Eight tracks run 74 minutes 25 seconds. Wikipedia lists Paul Neville guesting on guitar on "Man/Woman". Pitchfork gave it 7.9. Hydra Head later pressed a 1,000-copy double vinyl picture disc in February 2005.

In 2022 Broadrick called "Tired of Me" one of his most favorite songs, saying it captured the turmoil after Godflesh ended and a major relationship breakup.

years.cap: Justin Broadrick on guitar, Jesu live in Germany, May 3, 2005
years.h: Parsons and Dalton become the rhythm section
years.p: [[Ted Parsons|579dbbfe-100d-41b6-9ab7-4f7146c5d598]], who drummed in [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]] and [[Prong|366b86a0-74b2-4fcb-ba79-637258299dbb]], and Dalton turn into Broadrick's collaborators. Dalton's Wikipedia page dates the joining to 2005.
years.xp: Parsons already ran through Broadrick's past: Wikipedia says he played live drums for [[Godflesh|864aa861-e22a-4187-8baa-2ef0c215bc0a]] on the Songs of Love and Hate tour in 1996. Both men were on the December 2004 album, so the dates here are approximate.

years.cap: Justin Broadrick, Jesu live at Jail, Legnano, Italy, May 27, 2006
years.h: Silver swaps drone for shoegaze guitars
years.p: Four songs of layered guitar, and critics reached for My Bloody Valentine.

eras.title: Crossing the Atlantic
eras.text: Work permits eat three weeks of Jesu's first US tour, the splits start piling up, and a San Francisco show puts Mark Kozelek in the room.

years.cap: Justin Broadrick with Jesu, Shepherd's Bush Empire, London, 2007
years.h: Conqueror finally has a tune
years.p: Out on Hydra Head in February 2007, with Broadrick, Dalton and Parsons all playing. The drone of the debut gives way to song structure.

years.h: Work permits cost Jesu three weeks of the Isis tour
years.p: Jesu make their US live debut in March 2007 opening for Isis, with Danny Walker of Intronaut and Dave Cochrane standing in for Parsons and Dalton.
years.xp:
The Hydra Head Records SXSW showcase and the Isis dates were Jesu's first shows in the States. Wikipedia says Walker was a temporary touring drummer in March 2007, and that Phil Petrocelli took over the drums from late 2007.

Later that year the band headlined in the UK, Japan, Europe and the US.

years.h: Eluvium gets the other side of a Jesu 12"
years.p: Out July 5, 2007, the first of several Jesu splits.

years.h: Kozelek walks up to Broadrick after a San Francisco show
years.p: [[Mark Kozelek|99f4b23d-3711-4efe-ad71-9572158e234c]] saw Jesu play in 2007. It leads to a Jesu record on his label two years later, and an album together after that.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Kozelek was impressed by the set and approached [[Justin Broadrick|d547a180-6445-42e8-96d6-aabdb6425ab1]] afterward. In 2009 Kozelek's Caldo Verde label released Opiate Sun, and Broadrick interviewed Kozelek for the label's website.

In 2013 Kozelek covered the Godflesh song "Like Rats". Broadrick announced the joint album on April 27, 2015.

years.h: Pale Sketches and Lifeline land the same month
years.p: Pale Sketches is on Avalanche Records, Broadrick's own label. Lifeline is on Hydra Head in the US and Daymare in Japan.

years.h: Envy and Battle of Mice get a split each
years.p: The Envy split comes out July 11 on Daymare, the Battle of Mice split August 12 on Robotic Empire.

years.cap: Jesu live at All Tomorrow's Parties vs The Fans II
years.h: Why Are We Not Perfect?, with two covers in orbit
years.p: Out September 9, 2008 on Hydra Head. Around it, Jesu covered Pink Floyd's "Chapter 24" for a Syd Barrett tribute and The Cure's "The Funeral Party" for a Cure tribute.

eras.title: Ascension, mostly alone
eras.text: Parsons is the one other player left on record. Broadrick drifts toward electronics, announces a return to guitars, and gives each album years.

years.cap: Jesu at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, May 30, 2009
years.h: Infinity goes out on Broadrick's own label
years.p: Released July 23, 2009 on Avalanche Records, two months after Jesu played Primavera Sound in Barcelona.

years.h: Kozelek's Caldo Verde puts out Opiate Sun
years.p: The EP is Jesu's first release on the label run by [[Mark Kozelek|99f4b23d-3711-4efe-ad71-9572158e234c]] of [[Sun Kil Moon|ef2c6449-d02b-415b-ad8c-c14c08266552]].

years.h: Godflesh book Hellfest, and the electronics move to Pale Sketcher
years.p: Godflesh announced a reunion in November 2009 for Hellfest 2010. Broadrick said Jesu would head back to guitars.
years.xp:
Hellfest in Clisson, France, was Godflesh's first public reunion after eight years off. The electronic side of Broadrick's work went to Pale Sketcher.

Hydra Head reissued Heart Ache with the unreleased 2003 EP Dethroned as Heart Ache/Dethroned on November 16, 2010.

years.big: "I can't even sing the damn shit right live"
q: a downtuned Hüsker Dü or a downtuned Big Star or something like that.
years.h: Two years in the making, Ascension has Parsons on drums
years.p: Out May 10, 2011 on Caldo Verde. Broadrick plays the rest himself at Avalanche.
years.xp:
The pull line is Broadrick's, from a May 2011 interview with The Obelisk, where he explains why he prefers the studio. He said of the record, "I spent so long doing this record that this is the period where I usually kick the record to shit." Some of the songs had been around for "about the last two years."

His pitch for Jesu in the same interview: "a really guttural, low, heavy version of what I see as quite melancholic and beautiful pop songs."

years.h: Strings from Nicola Manzan, everything else from Broadrick
years.p: The five-song album, out September 23, 2013, was recorded at Avalanche.

eras.title: Kozelek's songs, Broadrick's guitars
eras.text: Two albums with Sun Kil Moon, then two more of his own on Bandcamp in 2020.

years.cap: Mark Kozelek of Sun Kil Moon on stage, Paris
years.h: Kozelek writes the songs, Broadrick builds the wall of guitar
years.p: [[Sun Kil Moon|ef2c6449-d02b-415b-ad8c-c14c08266552]] and Jesu release a joint album on Caldo Verde and Rough Trade on January 21, 2016, with Will Oldham, Rachel Goswell and Isaac Brock guesting.
years.xp:
It was recorded in Wales and the US, and members of Low play on it too. Pitchfork gave it 7.5 and it holds a 75 on Metacritic.

The pair played six shows in February and March 2016, with Steve Shelley of Sonic Youth on drums.

years.h: Kozelek and Broadrick go again
years.p: 30 Seconds to the Decline of Planet Earth, their second record together, comes out in May 2017.

years.h: Two albums on Bandcamp in one year
years.p: Never is out July 3, Terminus follows November 13.
